top_choice_rationale: P002 (Kane, Mele, Molenkamp) recognises a closed theory-to-experiment arc: the Z2 invariant and helical edge states of the quantum spin Hall effect, confirmed by quantised edge conduction in HgTe wells and reproduced for fifteen years. Band topology as an organising principle is the broadest conceptual result on the slate. The 2016 prize covered topological phase transitions and broken-time-reversal Hall states, so the physics is distinct. The omission of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang is a real cost that a narrow citation limits but cannot remove. P001 is a defensible, cleaner two-name alternative; P003 is promising but early, with the pairing mechanism unsettled.
recusal_note: No conflict on P002, P001 or P003 apparent from profile. As director of WACQT at Chalmers, with documented ties to Per Delsing and others linked to the 2025 circuit prize, I would recuse on circuit QED (B039), which is not on this slate.
